headlines.summary: 핵심요약 재정경제부, 최근 경제동향 6월호 발표 반도체·컴퓨터 수출 호황에 무역흑자 확대 취업자 4만명 감소·유가 급등에 민생 부담 가중 연합뉴스 우리 경제가 반도체를 중심으로 한 수출 호조에 힘입어 회복 흐름을 이어가고 있지만, 고용시장 둔화와 물가 상승이 겹치면서 체감경기 개선은 여전히 더딘 것으로 나타났다.

headlines.title: 기초대출, 하위 30%에 1000만원 … 성실 상환자는 기초저축 연계 추진
headlines.summary: ‘4대 기본금융’ 윤곽 드러나 도덕적 해이 방지도 논의중 소득 기준 하위 30%를 대상으로 최대 1000만 원의 자금을 빌려주는 기초대출과 기초보험 등 4대 기본금융이 윤곽을 드러내고 있다. 12일 더불어민주당과 신용회복위원회 등에 따르면 △대출 △보험 △저축 △채무조정·상담 등 4대 기초금융 상품 체계 마련을 위한 입법안이 오는 8월 발의될 예정이다.

headlines.title: 5대 은행 중기대출 1년새 17조 ↑… 연체율 상승은 부담
headlines.summary: 중소기업 대출 잔액 683조9138억원 월평균 취급액 李정부들어 5200억↑ 연체율 0.76%에서 0.92%로 치솟아 “갚지 않아도 된다는 인식 해소 중요” KB·신한·하나·우리·NH농협 등 5대 은행의 중소기업(개인사업자 포함) 대출 잔액이 최근 1년간 17조원 이상 증가한 것으로 나타났다.

headlines.summary: 전세 물량 감소에 가격도 올라 서울시 주택 공급 악순환 우려 전세난이 심화하면서 서울 지역 재개발·재건축 단지 이주대책에 비상이 걸렸다. 일부 지역에선 1000세대가 이사가야 하는데, 전세 매물은 수십개에 불과한 실정이다. 이주가 늦어지면 재개발 일정 차질이 불가피해지고 다시 전세 부족을 부르는 악순환을 부추길 것이라는 우려가 나온다.

headlines.title: 국세청, 교통과태료·개발부담금도 관리

headlines.title: ‘ 관세 직격탄 ’ 철강, 美 이어 핵심시장 유럽서도 ‘ 비명 ’
headlines.summary: EU, 관세 25→50% 인상 추진 무관세 수입 쿼터도 47% 줄여 유럽연합(EU)이 외국산 철강제품에 ‘무관세 할당량(쿼터)’을 줄이고, 관세율을 25%에서 50%까지 높이기로 하면서 국내 철강업계가 바짝 긴장하고 있다.

headlines.title: 역대급 수출에도 일자리 줄었다…뜻밖의 '고용 쇼크'에 경고
headlines.summary: 5월 뜻밖의 '고용 쇼크' 제조업서 14만개 감소 취업자 마이너스로 전환 역대급 수출에도 고용 역주행 고유가에 건설·서비스 직격탄 유례없는 반도체 수출 호황에도 국내 제조업 일자리가 7년 만에 최대 폭으로 감소했다. 중동 전쟁 장기화로 자동차, 고무·플라스틱 등 고유가 직격탄을 맞은 업종의 고용이 얼어붙었기 때문이다.

headlines.title: 고환율의 청구서 누구에게 향하나[ 조재연기자의 숫자 뒤의 사람들 ]
headlines.summary: 외환위기 때를 제외하면 과거엔 환율 전광판을 매일같이 들여다보는 사람이 그리 많지 않았다. 항공·운송·관광 등 환율에 민감한 업종에 종사하는 사람이거나 해외여행을 앞둔 사람, 유학생·주재원 등이 대부분이었다. 환율 변동의 일일 편차가 심하지 않기도 했거니와, 일상생활에서 환율이 직접 체감되는 경우가 많지 않았기 때문이다.

key_headlines.title: Claude AI Overtakes Google Gemini to Rank Second in Korea's Generative AI App Market
key_headlines.summary: Anthropic's Claude has surpassed Google's Gemini to become the second-largest generative AI app by revenue in South Korea, with the widening gap suggesting strong user preference shift away from the previous two-player market.

key_headlines.title: Gaon Electric Secures First Asian Certification for AI Data Center Cable Bus System
key_headlines.summary: Gaon Electric has obtained North American safety certification for its Cable Bus power transmission system for AI data centers, marking the first achievement by an Asian company in this high-value infrastructure sector.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's economy is showing recovery momentum driven by strong semiconductor and computer exports, with expanding trade surpluses and improving consumer and business sentiment. However, this positive trend is being tempered by rising inflation pressures stemming from Middle East tensions, with May oil prices surging 24.2% and unemployment affecting consumer confidence. The job market has weakened with 40,000 fewer jobs created in the latest period, and the government acknowledges that while exports are performing well, people's everyday economic burden is increasing due to price pressures and employment slowdown. The administration removed previous language about downside growth risks but emphasized concerns about inflation and employment as key challenges to monitor.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The government released its June monthly economic assessment noting that while exports and consumption show improvement, Middle East war-related uncertainties are creating significant inflation and employment challenges. The Korean won-dollar exchange rate has risen to around 1,560 won, with analysis suggesting the central bank may implement a 0.5 percentage point rate hike if it reaches 1,600 won to combat price pressures. The Bank of Korea faces a difficult balancing act between managing currency weakness and inflation while supporting employment and growth. Unemployment rose to 2.9%, up 0.1 percentage points year-over-year, as international oil prices and raw material costs have surged following Middle East developments.
sections.Financial Markets: The KOSPI recovered to 8,123.62, gaining 4.63% as foreign investors and institutions shifted to net buying while individuals engaged in profit-taking. The KOSDAQ also rebounded above 1,000 points as market volatility eased somewhat. Investors are positioning heavily in defensive stocks and semiconductor-focused ETFs as macroeconomic uncertainty persists, with particular interest in dividend-yielding defensive stocks that can withstand market turbulence. The upcoming US Federal Reserve FOMC meeting next week is expected to be a major determinant for further KOSPI gains, with peace talks between the US and Iran potentially reducing geopolitical risk premiums. Global investment firms like KKR maintain that Korean stocks remain undervalued despite recent market volatility.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea and Italy held a high-level business roundtable during President Lee Jae-myung's state visit, with Samsung Chairman Lee Jae-yong and other major executives participating alongside Italian counterparts to discuss cooperation in AI, semiconductors, automobiles, aerospace, clean energy, and biopharmaceuticals. Toyota is aggressively pursuing solid-state battery technology with plans for commercialization around 2027 and has secured approximately 1,000 related patents, while First Solar is acquiring a tandem cell startup, indicating intense global competition in next-generation battery technology. Gaon Electric became the first Asian company to obtain North American safety certification for Cable Bus systems used in AI data centers and large-scale industrial facilities. Korean companies like Samsung SDI are expanding battery partnerships with international firms including Stellantis.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul's apartment jeonse-to-sale price ratios hit 6-year highs, with Nowon reaching 55.5% and Dobong and Gangbuk exceeding 60%, reflecting concentrated demand in outer-ring neighborhoods as buyers seek to avoid speculative regulation areas. The Giheung area in Gyeonggi Province is emerging as a new hot spot, with national average apartment prices exceeding 1.5 billion won, driven by semiconductor company employee demand and bonus effects. A critical housing shortage is developing as 1,092 households need to relocate for redevelopment projects in Seoul but only 111 jeonse listings are available, threatening project timelines and creating a vicious cycle of housing supply constraints. Jeonse prices in Seoul rose 0.32% weekly in mid-June, the largest weekly increase in 11 years, as supply bottlenecks intensify.
sections.International Economy: The upcoming US Federal Reserve FOMC meeting next week is the key variable for global market direction, with markets expecting the Fed to maintain current rates under new Chair Kevin Wash rather than implement additional hikes. Peace negotiations between the US and Iran have progressed substantially, with potential resolution expected to reduce geopolitical risk premiums and stabilize oil prices, which would ease inflation concerns globally. Japan's central bank is also making policy decisions this week, adding to the macro event risk in global markets. South Korea's government indicated it may seek dialogue with the Trump administration on trade issues as the international trade order undergoes significant changes with new tariff implementations.
sections.AI & Economy: Claude, Anthropic's generative AI service, has overtaken Google Gemini to rank second in South Korea's generative AI app market by revenue, with the gap between Claude and Gemini widening significantly since late March. Credit card companies are intensifying competition to capture AI subscription users through cashback promotions, with Shinhan Card offering 4,000 won cashback for subscriptions over $5. Gaon Electric secured North American safety certification for AI data center Cable Bus systems, positioning Korean companies in the high-value infrastructure market serving the AI industry. Focus AI is restructuring its portfolio to concentrate resources on AI physical security solutions, divesting non-core assets to strengthen competitive positioning.
sections.Others: Seoul city approved Yongsan Electronics Market redevelopment as a key hub for AI and ICT content industries, transforming the historic electronics district into a center for emerging technology sectors. Retail companies are intensifying competition for 'home viewing' consumers during major sporting events like the World Cup, with large chains like Emart offering discounts on imported beer, chicken, sushi, and other popular home viewing food items. Credit card companies are launching promotional campaigns targeting subscription users of services like ChatGPT and Claude, reflecting the mainstream adoption of generative AI in consumer spending patterns. Elon Musk's capital raising through public offerings is expected to accelerate his ambitious projects ranging from electric vehicles to space data centers and Mars colonization initiatives.
